To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nature of embodiment in third wave design is collective and that the design of a digital musical instrument requires consideration of the instrument, musician and context as an ecology.

1) musical agency and an ecological view of DMIs are useful in developing an understanding of embodiment in third wave human-computer interaction; 2) the design of a DMI that supports musical agency is a process that requires a collective approach to embodiment, which includes a consideration of musicians, instrument, context, and audience.

(i) a collective notion of agency and embodiment is important in DMI design, (ii) a collective notion can be achieved by understanding the interrelationship between musician, instrument and audience, (iii) this inter relationship can be understood through an ecology of musical practice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how we might understand the nature of embodiment within third wave HCI.
the nature of musical embodiment in the context of DMI design.
the nature and role of embodiment within third wave HCI, specifically in the design of digital musical instruments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design of a musical instrument is a complex process that is influenced by many factors, some of which are not immediately obvious to those not involved in the process.

the project was successful in that it developed a practical understanding of musical agency and its ecology and that the resulting instrument is a useful tool in the hands of the musicians that were involved in the project.
the nature of embodiment is not a fixed concept and is dependent on the nature of the activity and the environment in which it takes place.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of the instrument and the design of the process were informed by a shared understanding of musical agency.
musical agency is the ability of a musician to create, express and communicate musical ideas through the use of a DMI, in the context of a performance.
the ecology of a DMI can only be understood by the musician who performs with it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a collective notion of musical agency is required to understand the breadth of considerations needed for a DMI.
embodiment should not be viewed as a property of the user and the device, but rather as an ecology of the user, device, context, audience and the creative practice itself.
the notion of embodiment needs to be understood in terms of a broader ecology of the musician, instrument, performance, context and audience.
